shortDescription: ROCHESTER, NEW YORK, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Syntec Optics Holdings, Inc. NASDAQ:OPTX, a pioneer in space, defense tech, and life sciences products, has secured $6.2 million in orders for its laser blood-test cartridges and optical reader subsystems. children: , a pioneer in space, defense tech, and life sciences products, has secured $6.2 million in orders for its laser blood-test cartridges and optical reader subsystems. Engineered for quick and ultra-precise critical care in every hospital and clinic worldwide, these products address a nearly $26 billion market that is projected to reach
Syntec's new cartridges are used, discarded, and replaced every 28 days across several life-threatening, high-acuity environments. This creates a steady, recurring, and consumable demand.
This one-minute blood test hardware is made for ICUs, Neonatal ICUs, operating rooms, and emergency departments—where survival depends on speed.
Syntec-enabled testing helps clinicians act before the following wide range of life-threatening emergencies escalate:
: Prevent severe tissue damage from anemia or carbon monoxide poisoning.
: Detect dangerous heart rhythm disturbances by measuring electrolytes.
: Catch and prevent severe low or high blood sugar issues.

The order brings the total life sciences backlog for production plan to nearly $90 million, including early detection of disease, surgical illumination and visualization, surgical robot connectivity, and DNA sequencing.

"Our established life sciences products diversify revenue and help clinicians save lives as we scale across many high-growth markets," said Dean Rudy, CFO of Syntec Optics. "During the pandemic, our bedside subsystems and cartridges delivered critical, hands-free respiratory metrics when minutes mattered most."
Syntec’s ongoing momentum directly aligns with the rapidly expanding global need for detection, sensing, and imaging capabilities.
Headquartered in Rochester, N.Y., Syntec Optics Holdings, Inc.

is one of the nation’s largest bespoke makers of high-precision optics. It pushes the limits of light-based technologies to connect and protect the world. Syntec supports critical missions ranging from low-Earth-orbit satellites to advanced next-gen connected-battlefield defense platforms, moon rocket actuators, AI data centers, and life sciences. As light-enabled technologies continue to account for a significant portion of global economic output—representing nearly $20 trillion of the $111 trillion in total worldwide production as of 2024—Syntec Optics remains positioned at the forefront of the modern optical revolution.
